leads.summary: Open shadows PR #13191 conflicts in both tooltip-sizing and surface-placement hunks
leads.consequence: #13191 reserves shadow extents in the popup and positions tooltipBubble at the left/top shadow inset; this PR reserves a hairline and instead anchors tooltipBubble to all four popup edges. The correct merge must reserve BOTH shadow extents and hairline, position the bubble inside the shadow and keep onAnchoring and the popup mask consistent. Choosing only the shadow hunk loses this PR's slack, choosing only this PR's hunk drops the shadow extents and its spec/mask. This is a source merge conflict, not proof either independently fails. An ordinary upstream merge cannot combine them automatically.

leads.summary: The new fixture stays green if the tooltip border is removed
leads.consequence: A plausible accidental deletion of the borderSpec binding (replace it with Border.none()) removes the visible tooltip border while preserving the three regex patterns. All assertions and the final pass remain green. Add an assertion on the tooltip's actual borderSpec/paint and, ideally, render an isolated popup at fractional scale; static width and margin patterns cannot establish that the border exists.

leads.summary: An accepted [spacing] scale=0 setting disables the new tooltip inset and slack
leads.consequence: A theme or user override setting [spacing] scale = 0 passes the Style parser's nonnegative validation. Style.spacing.hairline becomes 0, so both new + 2 * hairline reservations and the bubble's anchors.margins become zero. The tooltip border is again flush against the popup boundary on all bar orientations, defeating the intended clip clearance under the described fractional-scale mechanism (actual rendered clipping at zero scale was not captured). Use a nonzero device-pixel clearance independent of user-scaled spacing, or document and validate a positive minimum spacing scale.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (nit); published as Optional

leads.summary: Potential incompatible width bindings when combined with open fractional-border PR #10989
leads.consequence: The real merged source has both anchors.fill with 1px margins (this PR) and explicit width/height bindings to tooltipWindow.width/height (#10989). Qt's fill anchor sets the item size to parent size minus margins while the explicit bindings target full parent size. The two intents cannot both hold. Which wins after live popup resize or DPI transitions, and whether the stroke reaches the clip edge again, requires a Qt Quick/Quickshell runtime geometry trace. Both regex suites pass on the combined text, so they do not detect the disagreement. Coordinate one sizing rule with #10989.

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** The layout change is sound in the scope checked:
- `Style.spacing.hairline` is an `int` (`root.space(1)`, 1 at the default theme). The popup size therefore stays an integer.
- There is no binding loop. The popup's implicit size comes from the label's implicit size plus fixed padding and the hairline margins, never from the bubble's anchored size.
- The bubble stays centred on its target, with a transparent margin of one hairline on every side.

An offscreen Quickshell run with the real tooltip block (built-in default spacing and border values, device pixel ratio 1) gave:

| | popup | bubble x, y, width, height | right / bottom gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| merge base | 186 x 30 | 0, 0, 185.3125, 30 | 0.6875 / 0 |
| PR head | 188 x 32 | 1, 1, 186, 30 | 1 / 1 |

No QML binding-loop warnings appeared. The protective effect at fractional scales comes from source reading and a pixel model, not from a compositor run. That model follows Qt Wayland buffer rounding and Hyprland's edge crop on misaligned fractional-scale surfaces. In that model the border is never cropped at any modelled scale from 1.0 to 3, and from 1.25x upward at least one transparent device column or row remains between the border and the cropped edge.

### The new test exits 0 when its assertions fail

`test/shell.d/tooltip-border-stability-test.sh` has no `set -euo pipefail`, and its final `pass` line runs after `run_node_test`. When a Node assertion fails, the script still prints the final `ok` line and exits 0. Run against the merge base's `Bar.qml`:

```text
not ok - tooltip window reserves horizontal hairline slack
ok - Tooltip border keeps device-pixel slack at fractional scales
exit status: 0
```

Mutants of the head `Bar.qml` behave the same way: reverting the popup sizes or removing `anchors.margins` still exits 0. `test/shell` decides pass or fail by exit status, so it would count these runs as passed. Most Node-based tests in `test/shell.d/` start with `set -euo pipefail`.

**Impact:** The test prints `not ok` but cannot fail, so the runner never reports the regression it is meant to guard against.

**Suggested change:** Add `set -euo pipefail` after the shebang, or remove the trailing `pass` line. With either change, the test exits 1 on the merge base and 0 on the head.

**Optional test improvement:** The regexes match source text, not geometry. Two mutants still pass all three assertions. One moves `anchors.margins: Style.spacing.hairline` from the bubble to the label, which puts the bubble flush against the popup edge again. The other replaces the tooltip's `borderSpec` with `Border.none()`, which removes the border. A geometry assertion would catch the first case: bubble `x`/`y` equal to the hairline, and popup width minus bubble width equal to twice the hairline. That can be run in a Quickshell fixture, as in `button-border-stability-test.sh`.

### Other open PRs change the same tooltip bubble

- **#10989 and #12955** target the same symptom (open issue #10084, "Bar tooltip loses a border edge at display scale 1.25x (not 1.6x)"). They take the opposite approach: they bind `tooltipBubble` `width`/`height` to the full popup size, so the bubble is flush. Each merges cleanly with this PR as text. The result, however, gives the same item both `anchors.fill` with margins and explicit full-size `width`/`height` bindings, and each PR's test asserts its own layout. The merged tree was not run.
- **#13191** (theme-controlled shadows) changes the same two places. It adds shadow extents to the popup size and positions the bubble with `x`/`y` offsets. A three-way merge of the two `Bar.qml` changes onto `quattro` conflicts in both hunks.

**Impact:** With #13191, whichever lands later has to resolve the conflict by hand. With #10989 or #12955 there is no textual conflict, so the contradictory size rules could merge silently.

**Suggested change:** Reference issue #10084 in the PR description so maintainers can choose between this approach and #10989/#12955.

**Tooltip gap:** The `onAnchoring` offsets (`+ 6` / `- 6`) are measured to the popup edge, which now includes the transparent margin. The visible bubble therefore sits one hairline further from its target. In the offscreen run with a top bar, the bubble top moved from y 38 to 39. The other bar positions follow from the same code. Reducing each 6 px offset by one hairline keeps the previous spacing, if that matters.

**Optional:** `Style.spacing.hairline` scales with `[spacing] scale` and the font base size. At the default `[spacing] scale = 1.0` with font scaling on, it is 2 at `base-size` 18 to 29, which widens the margin and gap for no rendering reason. It is 0 with `[spacing] scale = 0`, which removes the protection. A fixed `1` would express one logical pixel of clearance directly.

**Description note:** At the merge base only the bubble's height matches the popup. It sits at (0, 0) with its own fractional width inside a `Math.ceil` popup. Qt draws a `Rectangle` border inside the item. The only edge-loss mechanism found in the source is compositor-side cropping of the popup surface; Qt does not draw outside it. The code change does not depend on this wording.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Pinned head `75b6507`, merge base equal to the current `quattro` tip. Source review of the tooltip block, `Style.qml`, Quickshell `PopupWindow` sizing, Qt Wayland buffer sizing and Hyprland surface cropping. Isolated runs of the new test, `border-geometry-test.sh` and `bar-test.sh` on head and merge base, test mutants, and an offscreen Quickshell geometry run at device pixel ratio 1. Fractional-scale behaviour is a source-based pixel model. No compositor or real fractional-scale rendering was run, and the reported symptom was not reproduced visually. The model reproduces thinning of the right border at 1.25x, but not its full loss.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
